messages:
maya: Heads-up — PR #9299 is ready but benches show a regression on longseq workloads (noticed this in the canary run).

maya: Key numbers vs main:
- p95: 120ms -> 160ms
- p99: 280ms -> 420ms
- memory: +420MB on 4k seq

maya: Artifacts: https://ci.redwood.local/builds/9299/bench-report.html and raw logs at https://s3.redwood/bench/9299/*.json

oliver: ack. thanks for the links. do we have the exact commit that introduced the change?

maya: it's the alloc-scheduler change in d3f4a1c — suggested by the allocator refactor (PR 9220). I re-ran with the new config toggles off and numbers look back to baseline.

sasha: can you paste the quick repro command you used for the canary? I'll run on my workstation.

maya: sure:
```bash
./bench/run_longseq.sh --model=gpt-small --seq=4096 --clients=16 --iters=200 --commit=d3f4a1c
```

rahul: curious if it's batching or prefill behavior. the allocator tweak changed placement thresholds so prefill may be getting split into smaller batches. that could bump overhead.

lin: i can run a sampling heap profile on the canary nodes if you want — will take ~20m to attach.

maya: please do, lin. attaching a heap + flamehelp would be helpful.

oliver: also canary-bot posted these traces: https://ci.redwood.local/canary/9299/traces — looks like increased tail on the scheduler queue.

canary-bot: canary run 9299 finished — status: degraded (p95 increased 33%). Artifacts: https://ci.redwood.local/canary/9299

rahul: tentative plan: hold merge until we either (a) add a guard in the allocator to preserve previous placement for longseq, or (b) make the new behavior opt-in behind a runtime flag and keep default as before.

sasha: +1 to a flag. quick patch to gate placement change should be small. if we push a fix, can we re-run canary in the same window?

maya: yes. i can spin a canary with the flag turned off and then with the small guard on to compare.

lin: started heap attach on canary-03 (pid 4218) — will upload profiles to the same artifacts link when done.

oliver: request: need 2 approvals for merge but let's not merge until we have a regression root cause or a mitigation. @rahul @sasha can you review the allocator guard patch when it's up?

rahul: will review, assigning myself to the fix.

sasha: will review too. if fix is trivial, we can fast-track once canary shows parity.

maya: thanks — holding merge and adding a note to the PR. tagging QA to run a quick throughput smoke after fix. :thumbsup:

canary-bot: canary run 9299-2 (with allocator flag disabled) finished — status: healthy (p95 within 2% of baseline). artifacts: https://ci.redwood.local/canary/9299-2

oliver: nice. once the guard patch lands and we get two approvals, we can merge.

maya: leaving an expected follow-up in the PR description documenting the benchmark results and the flag.

lin: uploaded heap + flame profiles to artifacts (heap-9299.tar.gz). initial glance shows increased small-allocation churn aligned with scheduler queue bursts. will post a summary in PR comments.

rahul: thanks. i'll open the guard PR now and ping for reviews.

maya: perfect — closing the loop here. will un-hold once rahul/sasha +1 and canary is green.

oliver: thanks everyone.
